_README: REAL Elementix payloads, captured verbatim from the live API on 2026-08-09.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The connector was written against GUESSED field names, and
its tests were written against the same guesses — so the tests passed while the
code could not read a single real record. A fixture invented by the same person
who wrote the reader proves only that they were consistent with themselves.
RULE: every test of a vendor reader reads from THIS file. Do not hand-write a
vendor row in a test. If a shape changes, re-capture it here from a live call
and let the tests fail until the reader is corrected — that failure is the
Trimmed to the fields the readers touch, plus the ones that previously misled.
Nothing is renamed; keys are exactly as the vendor sent them.

match_entity._note: SINGULAR `match` OBJECT — not an array, and not under any key rowsOf looked for. The name is `originalName`/`normalizedName`, never `name`.

get_entity_deeds._note: Envelope is {data, nextPage}. A ROW HAS NO `address` FIELD — it has `addresses[{id,addressFull}]`. The price is `totalConsideration` (never `consideration`) and the date is `recordingDate` (never `recordedDate`). `isGrantee`/`isGrantor` are computed SERVER-SIDE against the entity that was queried.

data._note: dataSource 'external' — the SAME transaction can appear again as 'elementix' with a different id. De-duplicate or one flip counts twice.

get_entity_mortgages._note: The amount is `mortgageAmount`, the parties are `borrowerNames` (not `borrowers`), and the term is `loanTermMonths`. `deedConsideration` is a STRING here while `totalConsideration` is a NUMBER on a deed. `loanPurpose:'refinance'` does NOT by itself mean an exit — a 10-month bridge can carry it.

data._note: Our own loan. `lenderName` 'YS Capital Group' — the short-term-loan test can read our own book directly.

get_person._note: CAPTURED LIVE 2026-08-18 (person MOTY BRISK / NJ, the owner's own screenshot). Envelope is a SINGULAR OBJECT under the key `person` — NOT a list, so lookups.rowsOf answers [] for it and the profile reads it directly. This one call carries the whole header: the counts the person page leads with (mortgageCount 349, deedCount 602, ownershipRecordCount 829, preforeclosureCount 3 — every one of them matching the screenshot) and currentExposure, WHICH IS A DECIMAL STRING, not a number.

get_person_entities._note: CAPTURED LIVE 2026-08-18. Envelope {data, nextPage} — and THERE IS NO TOTAL ON THE DATA CALL. `nextPage` present is the only signal that more exist, so "showing the first N of M" needs the separate scope:count call below.

get_person_entities_count._note: CAPTURED LIVE 2026-08-18 with scope:"count". {totalCount} — 295, matching the owner's screenshot. This is the ONLY way to size the entities tab, because get_person carries no entity count and the data call carries no total.

get_person_deeds._note: CAPTURED LIVE 2026-08-18. THE ADDRESS TRAP: on the PERSON deed tool `addresses` is an array of PLAIN STRINGS, while on the ENTITY deed tool (get_entity_deeds, above) the SAME field name is an array of {id, addressFull} OBJECTS. The person tool additionally carries `property_addresses` in SNAKE_CASE — and the person MORTGAGE tool spells the same idea `propertyAddresses` in camelCase and has no `addresses` key at all. One reader has to handle all of it; assuming any one spelling renders a blank column or [object Object].

get_person_mortgages._note: CAPTURED LIVE 2026-08-18. `mortgageAmount` is a DECIMAL STRING, not a number. There is NO `addresses` key here at all — the property is under `propertyAddresses` [{id, addressFull}], camelCase, where the deed tool used snake_case. `loanStatus` can be null even on a live loan, so an absent status is not evidence the loan is closed.

get_person_associated_people._note: CAPTURED LIVE 2026-08-18. Envelope {data, nextPage}. Counts are SHARED counts with the queried person, not that person's own totals.

get_person_cross_state._note: CAPTURED LIVE 2026-08-18. Envelope {data} with NO nextPage when the last page is reached. MOTY BRISK is three separate person records — NJ, FL, PA — which is the whole reason the profile merges across ids rather than filtering one id by state. EXACT-NAME matches only, so every row is a CANDIDATE and stays unconfirmed in elementix_person_aliases.

get_person_lender_network._note: CAPTURED LIVE 2026-08-18. THE ROWS ARE UNDER `lenderConnections`, a key lookups.rowsOf does not know — it would answer [] and the tab would render a confident zero for a person with seventy lenders. This is why every profile section declares its own rows key. Unpaged: the tool takes no page parameter and returned all seventy.

search_entity._note: search {query:'MW Trading LLC', entityFilter:'entity'} — captured live 2026-08-09. Envelope is {results, resultLimit:20}, NOT paginated. THE SAME NAME IS TWO ENTITIES IN TWO STATES (NJ and CA) — this is why match_entity requires a state, and why the no-state fallback must answer 'ambiguous' with the states named rather than pick. 'MW TRADING GROUP LLC' rides along in the same response: a near name is a DIFFERENT company and the exact-name filter must drop it. `highlightedName` carries HTML <mark> tags — never display it raw.

search_entity_state_filtered._note: The SAME query with state:'NJ' — captured live 2026-08-09 immediately after the one above. Exactly the one NJ company comes back (the CA twin and the FL near-name are both gone), which is what makes a per-state pull deterministic.

_state_required._note: PROVEN LIVE 2026-08-09 (the owner's own failed search): match_entity AND match_person called without `state` are refused whole — 'MCP error -32602: Input validation error … path: [state] … expected string, received undefined' — and the refused call still spends a slot of the shared hourly allowance. Entities and persons are keyed (name, state). The request contracts live in src/lib/elementix/request-contracts.json.

_documented_not_captured._note: Recorded in docs/research/elementix/04-connector-verification.md §14 from a live call by the verification research pass, but NOT re-captured here by hand. A reader for one of these must be proven against a fresh capture before it is trusted.
get_address_ownership_row_keys: entity_grantees[] (snake_case — the only one in the API)

_paging._note: PROVEN 2026-08-09: `get_entity_deeds` was called with {limit: 2} and returned FIVE rows. The page-size parameter is `perPage`; `limit` is ignored silently, and the default page is 5. A 29-property portfolio read through `limit` reads as five and nothing anywhere says so.

_param_names._note: PROVEN 2026-08-09: get_entity_deeds({entityId}) was REJECTED — 'Invalid arguments ... path: [id] ... expected string, received undefined'. The entity/address/person tools take `id`.
